What franchises actually changed/reinvented themselves for the better?
For me personally it has been the Zelda franchise.

Might & Magic. When it transitioned from grid based dungeons and overworld to total freedom of movement in Might & Magic 6 it was an enormous change. It also added realtime combat, 3d polygonal levels (although it stuck with sprites for NPCs), and I'm pretty sure it's system of upgrading classes and skills was new to the series as well. But I could be wrong about that last one. To this day Might & Magic 6 is one of my favorite RPGs ever, and certainly my favorite Might & Magic game.

And then there is the fact that Might & Magic is dead, and Heroes of Might & Magic is still around and kicking... sort of. Changing from an RPG into a strategy game is pretty big.

Warcraft has regrettably and permanently morphed into the MMO World of Warcraft. It definitely raised the Warcraft brand to new heights, and I'm pretty sure drove the popularity of Blizzcon, at least at one time if not still.
Ah... Heroes of Might & Magic. I hope that someday the IP will be bought by someone that can actually honor it.

A few years ago I would have said Resident Evil, but now I have to say they yo-yo'd on this. The re-release on Game Cube was exceptional, but not innovative for the franchise. But when they switched from fly-on-the-wall to over-the-shoulder, that was a huge change that was most certainly for the better. RE4 and even RE5 (if we disregard the goofy ending) were really fun. Since those, unfortunately, I feel the franchise has lost steam. With any luck though, they'll do a revamp of RE2 and get their shit back together.

Master of Orion series is another yo-yo. MOO2 was a major improvement on an already great base. The tech trees, tactical combat, structure building on planets, leaders, and race customization were huge improvements over Master of Orion 1, making MOO2 arguably the best game ever. Then came MOO3, which looked nice during battle, and that was about it. They fucked up the tech trees, made planet governors play the game for you, and obfuscated the mechanics so you never knew how anything actually worked.
